label: early original-phase input of 0/x/o/n/e/c/1/z
explanation: Fires almost entirely during the original (input) phase (96% of mass), concentrated at the first few positions: t=1 and t=2 hold ~76% of mass, t=3 14%, t=0 5%, and it is nearly silent from t>=4, on the delimiter, and in the copy phase. It is token-selective: the input token is usually one of 0, x, o (rate ~0.23-0.25, 5x lift), or n, e, c, 1, z (2-3x). It fires mostly on first occurrences of the token (92% of mass). The strongest activations are at t=2-3 on 0/x/n after a prefix of letters such as i, v, b (e.g. i i d [0]). The predicate (early original step AND input in that token set) gets dev F1 0.59, recall 0.80, mass recall 0.87. Precision is only ~0.47, because the same tokens at early positions often do not fire, depending on the earlier tokens in some way I could not capture; adding a seen() filter on earlier tokens or requiring in_first did not help. The missed activations are low-magnitude: other tokens such as f, w, q early on, plus a scattering in the copy phase.
